subtype: Approach: choosing a fancy project he cannot finish [Pitfall]
passage: I'm Lalit. When I saw my friend Gurleen's volcano at the school fair last year, with red lights and a rumbling sound from a speaker, I wanted one better. I told the teacher I would make a volcano that worked, with lights, smoke and sound. I drew the plan in one evening. Then I found out I had only one small battery, no wire and two weeks. I glued the cone on the first day, but the sound never worked and the lights would not stay on. The night before the fair, the volcano sat half-painted on my desk. Gurleen's was better than ever. I stood there with my hands empty.

qa.q: What did Lalit tell the teacher would be made?
qa.a: Lalit said a volcano that worked, with lights, smoke and sound.

qa.q: How did Lalit feel the night before the fair?
qa.a: Lalit felt disappointed and probably embarrassed, with the volcano half-painted and the others ready. 😔

qa.q: What alternative approach could Lalit use, and why?
qa.a: Lalit could choose a simpler project that fits the time and materials or check the plan with the teacher first. A finished small project beats a half-done big one.

qa.q: How might Gurleen see the fair, with a volcano that turned out so well?
qa.a: Gurleen's volcano was better than ever, so Gurleen probably feels proud of it and may not know how hard the night before was for Lalit.

grounding: Lalit chooses a fancy volcano project like a friend's, cannot finish it in the time and materials available, and it stays half done.

subtype: Approach: choosing a fancy project he cannot finish [Pitfall]
passage:
Parent's note to the science teacher, with Varun's project
Ma'am, Varun wanted to explain why his volcano model is unfinished. Three weeks ago he saw his friend's volcano with lights and a smoke machine on a video and wanted one just like it. He planned a papier-mache mountain, red lights inside, a sound box and bubbling lava. He spent the first week only on the mountain. The lights needed a battery holder we didn't have. The sound box never worked. By Sunday night the lava part was still in a bag. He was very upset and cried. We talked about choosing something he could finish. He is bringing the mountain as it is, and he wants to tell you what he learnt.
- Madhuri

qa.q: What part of the volcano was still in a bag on Sunday night?
qa.a: The lava part was still in a bag.

qa.q: How did Varun feel on Sunday night?
qa.a: He was very upset and cried, seeing the project was not going to be finished.

qa.q: Which approach would have suited Varun better, and why?
qa.a: Choosing a simpler project that fits his time and materials, like just the lava reaction, because a finished small project beats an unfinished big one.

qa.q: How does the unfinished project look to Madhuri?
qa.a: Madhuri sees the effort and the disappointment and wants the teacher to understand, while hoping he learns to choose something he can finish.

grounding: It shows a child choosing a fancy volcano like a friend's, running out of time and materials, and leaving it half done.

subtype: Approach: choosing a fancy project he cannot finish [Pitfall]
passage:
Sunday night
Diary, the science fair is tomorrow and my project is a mess. I wanted to make a robot arm that picks things up, like the one Kavitha's cousin made. I told everyone. I bought nothing and planned everything. First the syringes didn't fit the pipes. Then the cardboard bent. Then I needed glue that dries fast and we didn't have it. So now I have an arm that goes up but not down. Mummy said, "Yogesh beta, next time pick something you can finish in the time you have." I know. I just wanted something that looked amazing. Now it looks broken. I'm taking it anyway.
- Yogesh

qa.q: What did Yogesh want the robot arm to do?
qa.a: Yogesh wanted it to pick things up.

qa.q: How did Yogesh feel on the night before the fair?
qa.a: Yogesh felt disappointed and embarrassed, since the project that was meant to look amazing now looked broken.

qa.q: What would you change first if you were Yogesh, and why?
qa.a: Start with a simpler goal, like an arm that only lifts, and add parts only if there is time, so something works by the fair.

qa.q: How does the project look to Mummy?
qa.a: Mummy sees an unfinished project and gently gives advice about choosing something that fits the time, without scolding.

grounding: It shows a child choosing a fancy robot arm project that could not be finished in time, running out of materials and ending with a half-done model.
